scope: Native regression triage and independently adjudicated primitive proofs; no full substrate or eleven-substrate acceptance.

redPressureTests.genericRuntimeDeficiency: The isolated subprocess environment lacks a trusted machine application-data location needed by an installed discovery helper. Current native invocation tests fail while provisioning the fixture, before compilation, transport dispatch or semantic verification.
redPressureTests.reusablePrimitive: Explicit immutable typed known-host-location context with an isolated default, closed roles and caller-controlled attenuation. Designed; production Foundation implementation is not yet demonstrated.
redPressureTests.thinProviderSpecificLayer: The installed compiler-discovery query requests only the machine application-data role. The read-only seven-profile counterfactual finds ProgramData alone sufficient on this runner. It neither grants arbitrary environment inheritance nor changes any production invocation.
redPressureTests.greenEvidenceRequired: Actual Foundation/BoundedCapabilityProcess counterfactual and unchanged three invocation-binding tests must pass on the current source, followed by the full native Windows suite, release build and canonical seven-operation provider proof.
redPressureTests.makesOtherSubstratesEasier: Potentially: a generic constrained host-context contract can serve native client discovery for Linux, Kafka, Kubernetes and WASM. Cross-substrate support and authority/cache identity binding are not demonstrated.

redPressureTests.genericRuntimeDeficiency: Timestamp-based snapshot identity verification currently uses a test filesystem operation that fails natively with Cocoa257. The runtime cache property must still be verified without changing its identity semantics or dropping denial assertions.
redPressureTests.reusablePrimitive: Portable timestamp fixture handling and exact current-byte/incarnation verification, preserving cache withdrawal, budget and race checks.
redPressureTests.thinProviderSpecificLayer: A Windows-compatible filesystem timestamp update in the fixture; no provider-specific runtime tool.
redPressureTests.greenEvidenceRequired: Import the reviewed portable fixture repair into the current candidate and rerun all five snapshot-pool tests and the full current native suite.
redPressureTests.makesOtherSubstratesEasier: Yes for reusable byte-identity cache verification and portable tests; no new substrate integration is implied.

redPressureTests.genericRuntimeDeficiency: The genuine receipt rotation test fixture currently applies a filesystem permission operation unsupported on the native test host, yielding Cocoa513 before receipt effects or trust decisions.
redPressureTests.reusablePrimitive: Portable private fixture/export handling plus issuer lifecycle receipt verification against independent provisioned public pins. The reviewed repair does not weaken trust policy or assertions.
redPressureTests.thinProviderSpecificLayer: Platform-correct private fixture creation and metadata handling; cryptographic trust rules remain generic.
redPressureTests.greenEvidenceRequired: Apply the reviewed fixture repair to the current candidate; actual native rotation test, independently verified two receipts and all thirteen trust decisions must pass again on that source.
redPressureTests.makesOtherSubstratesEasier: Yes: portable native trust verification can be reused across all substrates. External issuer authority and delegation remain separate acceptance requirements.

limits: This is a controlled genuine private Linux D-Bus proof.
Four dispatch rows are not four durable writes.
Old effect marker rejection is for a new task, not reuse of one authority lease.
No issuer authority envelope, external issuer identity or complete full-runtime acceptance is demonstrated.
